steps: Use day-old cooked white rice for best results; jasmine is the rice this dish is made with.
Peel and devein the shrimp. Mince the garlic, cut the tomato into wedges, slice the green onion, and cut the cucumber into rounds to serve raw alongside.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wok over high heat and fry the garlic for about 20 seconds until fragrant.
Add the shrimp and toss constantly until just pink, then push them to one side of the wok.
Crack the egg into the empty side and scramble it, breaking it apart as it sets.
Add the rice and stir-fry hard, pressing out any clumps, then fold in the tomato and green onion.
Season with the fish sauce, the soy sauce for colour, the sugar, salt and white pepper, and toss until everything is coated.
Plate with the cucumber slices and a lime wedge to squeeze at the table, and add sliced serrano chile to taste.

note: Kept the Thai label and fixed it into khao phad goong: Sesame Oil and Green Peas out (Chinese-American frozen-veg signature), Vegetable Oil + Garlic + Tomato + Green Onion + Fish Sauce + Sugar in, Soy Sauce cut 12->5g as a colour note, raw Cucumber and a Lime wedge added as the standard service; Chili Flakes -> Serrano Chile (fresh chili stand-in for Thai chili). +41 cal.

steps: Cook the white rice according to package directions; jasmine is the rice this dish is served with.
Pound or mince the garlic together with the serrano chile into a rough paste.
Hand-chop the chicken thigh coarsely rather than dicing it, since the loose uneven texture is part of the dish.
Heat most of the vegetable oil in a wok over high heat, add the garlic and chile paste, and fry about 20 seconds until fragrant.
Add the chicken and stir-fry hard until browned and crisp at the edges.
Season with the fish sauce, the soy sauce for colour, the sugar, salt and white pepper, and toss to coat.
Kill the heat and fold in the basil, letting the residual heat wilt it rather than cooking it; holy basil is what the dish wants.
In a separate pan fry the egg in the remaining vegetable oil over high heat until the white is crisp at the edges and the yolk is still runny.
Serve the chicken over the rice with the fried egg on top.

note: Fixed the headline data bug: a dish named for basil now contains Basil 20g. Bell Pepper (Chinese-American) and Sesame Oil out; Vegetable Oil, Fish Sauce and a fried Egg (kai dao) in; Soy Sauce 12->6g as dark-soy colour only; Chili Flakes -> Serrano Chile 3g. +93 cal (+16%), +6g protein, driven by the egg.

steps: Dry-toast 8 g of the raw white rice in a pan over medium heat until deep golden and nutty, then grind it coarsely; this is khao khua, the toasted rice powder that gives larb its texture.
Cook the remaining white rice according to package directions to serve alongside.
Mince the chicken breast finely by hand.
Cook the minced chicken in a splash of water over high heat, stirring to keep it loose, until just cooked through; larb meat is simmered in a little liquid, never fried in oil.
While the chicken is still warm, toss it with the lime juice, fish sauce, sugar, salt and the toasted chili flakes.
Fold in the sliced shallot, green onion, cilantro, mint and the khao khua.
Spoon into romaine lettuce cups and serve with the rice on the side.

note: Rebuilt the non-dish (a P.F. Chang's-lineage Chinese-American invention filed under Thai) into Larb Gai, keeping the minced-chicken / lettuce-cup / rice-side structure. Coleslaw Mix, Carrot and Soy Sauce out; Fish Sauce, Shallot, Green Onion, Cilantro, Sugar and Mint in; khao khua toasted from 8g of the existing rice. Also fixes the phantom frying oil, since larb meat is water-cooked. Net roughly flat on calories.

steps: Cook the white rice according to package directions; Thai food is eaten with jasmine rice, not brown rice.

Mix the sauce in a bowl first, as Thai cooks do, so it goes into the wok as one splash: fish sauce, soy sauce, sugar, salt, white pepper and the sesame oil, which belongs in the sauce rather than in the hot wok.
Peel and devein the shrimp. Mince the garlic, slice the bell pepper and carrot, and shred the cabbage.
Get the wok very hot, add the vegetable oil, then the garlic for about 20 seconds until golden.
Add the shrimp and toss continuously until just pink, then lift them out.
Stir-fry the carrot and cabbage first, then the bell pepper, for 2-3 minutes, keeping everything crisp.
Return the shrimp, pour in the sauce, and toss to coat.
Off the heat, add the green onion and sliced serrano chile to taste, then serve over the rice.

note: Renamed off the English description to the real dish, pad pak ruam mit goong. Brown Rice -> White Rice (jasmine) and Zucchini (Mediterranean) -> Cabbage standing in for napa; Garlic, Vegetable Oil, Fish Sauce, Green Onion and Sugar added; Soy Sauce 12->6g and Sesame Oil 5->2g demoted into the pre-mixed sauce, added off-heat. +72 cal (+15%). Oyster sauce is not in the frozen vocabulary, so the sauce leans on fish sauce, soy and sugar.

steps: This is an honest weeknight shortcut broth, not a from-scratch pho: real pho bo simmers beef bones for six hours or more, and good store-bought beef broth stands in for that here.
Char the onion and the ginger directly over a flame or under the broiler until blackened in patches, then scrape off the worst of the char.
Dry-toast the star anise, cinnamon, cardamom and coriander in a dry pan until fragrant, about 2 minutes, then tie them in a spice bag or a square of cheesecloth.
Simmer about 2 cups of beef broth, uncovered, with the charred onion and ginger and the spice bag for 30-40 minutes.
Season the broth with the fish sauce, sugar and salt, tasting as you go.
Cook the rice noodles, the flat banh pho, according to package directions, drain, and put them in the bowl.
Slice the beef sirloin paper-thin against the grain and fan the raw slices over the noodles.
Strain the broth and pour it boiling over the beef; the heat cooks the thin slices through.
Serve with the bean sprouts, basil, cilantro, green onion and a lime wedge on a plate alongside, added at the table.

note: Broth repair: Garlic (not a pho aromatic), Soy Sauce (a Chinese seasoning) and Spinach (appears in no pho) out; Fish Sauce, Sugar, Bean Sprouts, Basil, Cilantro and Green Onion in; Ginger 5->10g and now charred with the onion. Spice sachet went from one cinnamon stick to toasted Star Anise + Cinnamon + Cardamom + Coriander; Black Pepper dropped. Also rescaled the hard-coded '3 cups' liquid to about 2 cups for one bowl. Net ~+21 cal.

steps: Char the onion and the ginger over a flame or under the broiler until blackened in patches; charred ginger is the aromatic that makes this pho ga rather than plain chicken soup.
Dry-toast the coriander, star anise and cinnamon until fragrant and tie them in a spice bag; the spicing here is deliberately lighter than in beef pho.
Simmer about 2 cups of chicken broth with the charred aromatics and the spice bag, poaching the chicken breast in it for 12-15 minutes until just cooked through.
Lift the chicken out and hand-shred it rather than slicing it into strips, then let the broth carry on simmering another 15-20 minutes.
Season the broth with the fish sauce, sugar and salt.
Cook the rice noodles separately according to package directions and drain.
Put the noodles in the bowl, pile the shredded chicken over them, and ladle the broth through a strainer.
Serve with the bean sprouts, cilantro, green onion, basil and a lime wedge alongside, added at the table.

note: Same broth repair as Beef Pho plus the recipe-specific fix: Ginger 10g added and charred (it was missing entirely, while Beef Pho beside it had it). Garlic and Spinach out; Fish Sauce, Sugar, Bean Sprouts, Cilantro, Green Onion and Basil in. Spices go to toasted Coriander + Star Anise + Cinnamon, kept lighter than pho bo; Black Pepper dropped. Chicken is now poached and hand-shredded. '3 cups' liquid rescaled to about 2 cups. Net ~+27 cal.

steps: Julienne the carrot and daikon and quick-pickle them in the rice vinegar with a little of the sugar and a pinch of salt for 30 minutes; this is do chua.

Whisk the nuoc cham: fish sauce, lime juice, the rest of the sugar, a splash of warm water, minced garlic and sliced serrano chile, tasting until it balances sour, salty and sweet. This dressing is the dish, not a condiment on the side.
Set a spoonful of the fish sauce and garlic mixture aside and marinate the shrimp in it for 15 minutes.
Cook the rice noodles, the round bun vermicelli, then drain, rinse cold and drain well.
Grill or sear the shrimp over high heat until charred at the edges.
Fry the sliced shallot in the vegetable oil until golden and crisp and drain it, then stir the green onion into a little of the warm oil to make scallion oil.
Build the bowl: shredded romaine lettuce and bean sprouts at the bottom, cold noodles over them, then the cucumber, the pickled carrot and daikon, mint and cilantro.
Top with the grilled shrimp, the scallion oil and the crispy fried shallots, which are the traditional nut-free crunch here.
Pour the nuoc cham over at the table and toss everything together.

note: Renamed to Bun Tom Nuong (bun tom alone is a shrimp noodle soup). Added the two things that define a bun bowl: nuoc cham (Fish Sauce + Lime + Sugar + Garlic + chile) and do chua (Carrot + Daikon quick-pickled in Rice Vinegar), plus Bean Sprouts, Mint, Cilantro, scallion oil and crispy fried Shallot as the nut-free crunch. Nothing was removed. Largest macro swing in the slice: 305 -> ~417 cal (+36%), protein flat; report explicitly justifies it and names the fried shallot as the droppable part.

originalName: Five-Spice Duck Stir Fry with Rice

recipe.name: Five-Spice Duck Stir Fry with Rice

steps: Cook the white rice according to package directions.

Slice the duck breast thinly against the grain and marinate it for 15 minutes in half the cornstarch, half the dry sherry, a little of the soy sauce, the five-spice and the white pepper; this is velveting, and the marinade is where five-spice belongs rather than as a dry rub.
Mix the sauce separately: the hoisin sauce, the remaining soy sauce and dry sherry, the sugar, the salt, and the rest of the cornstarch slaked in a spoonful of cold water.
Mince the garlic and grate the ginger.
Get the wok smoking hot, add the vegetable oil, then the garlic and ginger for 20-30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the duck, spread it in a single layer and let it sear before tossing, 2-3 minutes.
Add the shredded cabbage and stir-fry 2 minutes, keeping it crisp.
Pour the sauce down the side of the wok and toss until it thickens and glosses the duck.
Off the heat, toss through the green onion and the sesame oil, which is a finishing oil here, then serve over the rice.

note: Duck Leg -> Duck Breast (leg is a braising cut; it cannot be stir-fried in 3 minutes). Added Cornstarch for velveting and the sauce slurry, Dry Sherry as the Shaoxing-wine stand-in, Hoisin Sauce as the oyster-sauce stand-in, Vegetable Oil for the wok, Sugar; Broccoli and Bell Pepper (takeout vegetables) -> Cabbage, Green Onion 15->30g; Sesame Oil demoted to a 3g off-heat finish; Black Pepper dropped (Chinese cooking uses white). Only +28 cal because duck breast is leaner than leg in this registry.

steps: Score the duck breast skin in a crosshatch without cutting into the meat, and season it with the salt and white pepper.
Place the duck skin-side down in a cold, dry pan and bring it up to medium heat, rendering for 6-8 minutes until the fat has run out and the skin is deep golden and glassy.
Flip the duck for 2 minutes, rest it 5 minutes, then slice it thinly.
Cut the cucumber into thin batons and the green onion into long fine julienne strips to match.
Warm the flour tortilla in a dry pan for 30 seconds per side; it stands in for the thin steamed Mandarin pancakes.
Smear the tortilla with the hoisin sauce, lay on the duck, cucumber and green onion, roll and serve.

note: Best recipe in the slice, three small fixes. Garlic and Ginger removed (Cantonese stir-fry aromatics in a Beijing roast; Peking duck's accompaniments are only pancake, sweet sauce, cucumber, scallion). Duck Leg -> Duck Breast with the cold-pan render, which is the only way the crisp-skin technique the steps already describe actually works. Whole Wheat Tortilla -> Flour Tortilla, now that a plain one exists in the registry. Black Pepper -> White Pepper. -94 cal (-11%).
